title: Borrowed data stays a placeholder
statement: Mark data borrowed from another group of students, such as another grade's weak skills, as a placeholder, never as measured for the students in hand.
example: Until its own data arrived, one new grade's generator could target the earlier grade's three weak skills only as a flagged placeholder.
detail: The generator harness for a new grade lists the cohort data that must come from that grade and must not be made up (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/courses/g5-reading/generator/G5_GENERATOR.md`). Until the new grade's weak-skill data lands, it targets the earlier grade's weak skills as a marked placeholder, explicitly flagged and never presented as measured, and it must not reuse the earlier grade's test norms of 186.6, 193.9 and 197.1 (the same file).

evidence.quote: **G5 cohort numbers are TO-SOURCE, NOT invented.**

target the G3 weak-skills — compare/contrast, cause/effect, sequence — as a *marked placeholder*, explicitly flagged, never presented as measured G5 data); **G5 MAP norms** (do NOT reuse G3's 186.6 / 193.9 / 197.1);

The G2 BrainLift v0.1 inherited G3's premise — *students pass internal mastery but stay flat on MAP (a test-rigor problem)*. We then pulled the live G2 data (1,597 students, `rpt2_*` views, 2026-06-23). **The premise does not hold for G2.**
The students who pass our internal test **transfer well** (85th percentile). The rigor gap is ~8 students. The premise is refuted for G2.

The "EGM=0 / students can't pass grade-level tests" premise that the original build rested on was **falsified by the team's own data**: passing is rare because of *non-participation*, not test failure.
